6	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A name made only of replaced or trailing characters gives a folder name ending in a space**\n\n`validateWorkspaceName` accepts a name like `?`, `...` or `-`. In `newWorkspaceFolderName`, `?` turns into `-`, and the trailing-strip regex then removes it, so `safe` ends up as `\"\"`. The function then returns `\"Kaipu Record — \"`, which ends in a space: the same trailing space the doc comment says Windows refuses. On macOS a second name like that (for example `*`) collides with the first folder, and `create` refuses it as `exists`. A possible fix: when `safe` is empty, fall back to a placeholder, or strip the trailing space from the whole result. Another option is to reject such names in validation.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",
7	    "replies": [
8	      {
9	        "author": "csdev19",
10	        "body": "Fixed in 886d67f0. Runs of unsafe characters now become one dash and only dots and spaces are stripped from the end, so `?` gives `Kaipu Record — -`. A name that leaves nothing (`...`) falls back to `workspace`. Tests in `workspace-name.test.ts` check the folder name never ends in a space. `?` and `*` still map to the same folder; `create` then refuses the second as \"exists\" and the dialog says so, which I think is the right outcome."

18	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Edit rollback leaves a newly written identity.json when the folder had none before**\n\nWhen the registry write fails, the rollback only restores the folder's file if `previous.kind === \"ok\"`. Take a pending entry whose folder is reachable but has no `identity.json` (`previous` is missing). `edit` writes a fresh identity at line 581 with the entry's id and the new name. If `update` then throws, that file stays on disk. The next probe finds an identity with the matching id and adopts it, so the change that was refused shows up again. Calling `removeIdentity(entry.path)` in the non-ok case would undo it the way `create`'s `undo` does.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

22	        "body": "Fixed in 886d67f0: the rollback also calls `removeIdentity` when the folder had no file. In practice the probe at the start of `edit` rewrites a missing identity first, so `previous` is normally `ok` by then; I added a test for that real path (the old file is back after a failed registry write) and kept the `absent` branch as the guard for the race."

42	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Edit does not re-check name uniqueness inside the locked write, unlike create**\n\n`create` re-runs `validateWorkspaceName` inside `update`, so two concurrent creates cannot take the same name (line 515). `edit` validates only once, at line 540, before several awaits (the probe, `readIdentity`, `writeIdentity`). The same `NameTakenError` re-check inside the `update` callback would close this gap.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

66	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: The stale-answer test would still pass without the `alive` guard**\n\nAfter `answerFirst(...)`, the test waits for one `await Promise.resolve()` and then checks that the \"Wo\" path is absent. If the `alive` guard in `workspace-dialog.tsx:83` were removed, the late `.then` would call `setLocation` outside `act`. React schedules that render through its scheduler, not inside the same microtask, so `queryByText(...Wo)` would still return null and the test would pass anyway. To make the test catch the bug, wait for any pending render before the assertion, for example `await act(async () => answerFirst(...))`, or assert inside a `waitFor` that runs after a macrotask, and keep checking that the \"Work\" path is still shown.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

90	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Change folder… refuses the moved folder of a `pendingInit` workspace, which is the case it is meant to fix (confidence medium)**\n\n`open()` registers the migrated Default workspace with `pendingInit` when the old `vaultDirectory` is unplugged at upgrade (lines 298-303). The folder has `.kaipu/` sidecars and no identity, so `checkRelocate` reaches line 809 and returns `has-items-no-identity`. The user is told the folder \"isn't one of your workspaces\" and cannot repoint it.\n\nThe same rule hits a `pendingInit` entry whose moved folder already holds an identity with another id. Line 802 refuses it as `different`, but `availability` adopts that id at lines 678-687.\n\nA possible fix: when `entry.pendingInit` is set, accept a folder with no identity (the probe writes it later). For a folder with another workspace's identity, apply the same `pendingInit && !this.get(identity.id)` adoption rule that `availability` uses.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

102	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Relocating the active workspace throws away a pending quiet capture that could still be saved (confidence medium)**\n\n`relocateActive` calls `dropPendingCaptures()`, which dismisses the capture toast and clears the retained PNG (`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/index.ts:975-978`). findings.title: The part that silences the toast has no test
findings.body: `relocate.test.ts:158` pins the `unchanged` flag in main. Nothing covers the other two links: `index.ts:349` copying the flag into the IPC result, and `onRelocated` returning early at line 168 (the dialog tests only mock `onRelocated`). If either link were dropped, the "now points to the new folder" toast would come back and every test would still pass. A small test of `WorkspacesProvider`'s `changeFolder` with a relocate result carrying `unchanged: true` that asserts no toast would pin the user-visible behavior.

contracts.action: Picking the folder the workspace already points at in "Change folder…" returns an `unchanged` result, and the renderer skips the toast
contracts.equivalent_path: The original relocate path (`registry.relocate` or `relocateActive`) for a different folder; it shows the `folderChanged` toast via `onRelocated`.
contracts.before_after: Before: `checkRelocate` runs, then an early return with the current entry when the paths match. After: the same early return, now with `unchanged: true`. `relocateFolder` still runs `reg.availability`, `refreshTitles` and `broadcastState` after it (index.ts:342-345), so the probe still rewrites a deleted identity file. `onRelocated` returns before `showToast` when the flag is set (workspaces-context.tsx:168).
contracts.visible_effect: No toast and no window prompt. The dialog's `onRelocated` call (workspace-dialog.tsx:145) and Settings' `changeFolder` (workspaces-context.tsx:184-185) both go through the same `onRelocated`, so both stay silent.
contracts.failure_mode: The path comparison uses `resolve()` and is case-sensitive. On a case-insensitive macOS volume, picking the same folder with different casing misses the early return and runs the full transaction, which is the old behavior and harmless. No new async call is added.

contracts.action: An offline edit of a `pendingInit` workspace now keeps `pendingInit`
contracts.equivalent_path: `create` and the earlier `edit` code, which cleared `pendingInit` unconditionally.
contracts.before_after: Before: `edit` always deleted `pendingInit`. After: it deletes it only when `savedToFolder`. Otherwise `pendingIdentity` is set (line 638), and `availability` writes the identity once the folder is back. `checkRelocate` can still accept the moved folder for a `pendingInit` entry, per the earlier thread.
contracts.visible_effect: Renaming while the drive is away no longer makes "Change folder…" refuse the moved folder. The registry-relocate test covers this path.
contracts.failure_mode: The edit's own failure paths are unchanged: a failed identity write returns `not-writable`, and a failed registry update rolls the folder back.

thread_replies.reply: Addressed. `relocate.ts:44` returns `unchanged: true`, `index.ts:349` passes it through the IPC result, and `onRelocated` (`workspaces-context.tsx:168`) returns before the toast. Both the dialog and Settings go through `onRelocated`, so both stay silent. Only the main-side flag has a test; the renderer skip does not (noted as a finding).

Addressed. When the picked folder is the one the workspace already uses, `relocateWorkspace` returns before `relocateActive` (`relocate.ts:43-45`), so no window is asked to save and the generation stays. `relocate.test.ts:156-161` checks both.

input.summary: The change does what the PR says. Picking the folder a workspace already uses now returns an `unchanged: true` flag, and that flag passes through the IPC result to `onRelocated`, which shows no toast. The `pendingInit` fix in `edit` keeps the flag when the identity was not written to the folder, and a new test covers it. I found no defects. One minor gap remains: nothing tests the renderer skip or the `index.ts` passthrough of `unchanged`. Two earlier threads (4439336705 and 4439290177) are addressed by the current code.

contracts.equivalent_path: The original relocate path (`registry.relocate` or `relocateActive`) for a different folder; it shows the `folderChanged` toast via `onRelocated`.
contracts.before_after: Before: `checkRelocate` runs, then an early return with the current entry when the paths match. After: the same early return, now with `unchanged: true`. `relocateFolder` still runs `reg.availability`, `refreshTitles` and `broadcastState` after it (index.ts:342-345), so the probe still rewrites a deleted identity file. `onRelocated` returns before `showToast` when the flag is set (workspaces-context.tsx:168).
contracts.visible_effect: No toast and no window prompt. The dialog's `onRelocated` call (workspace-dialog.tsx:145) and Settings' `changeFolder` (workspaces-context.tsx:184-185) both go through the same `onRelocated`, so both stay silent.
contracts.failure_mode: The path comparison uses `resolve()` and is case-sensitive. On a case-insensitive macOS volume, picking the same folder with different casing misses the early return and runs the full transaction, which is the old behavior and harmless. No new async call is added.

contracts.action: An offline edit of a `pendingInit` workspace now keeps `pendingInit`
contracts.equivalent_path: `create` and the earlier `edit` code, which cleared `pendingInit` unconditionally.
contracts.before_after: Before: `edit` always deleted `pendingInit`. After: it deletes it only when `savedToFolder`. Otherwise `pendingIdentity` is set (line 638), and `availability` writes the identity once the folder is back. `checkRelocate` can still accept the moved folder for a `pendingInit` entry, per the earlier thread.
contracts.visible_effect: Renaming while the drive is away no longer makes "Change folder…" refuse the moved folder. The registry-relocate test covers this path.
contracts.failure_mode: The edit's own failure paths are unchanged: a failed identity write returns `not-writable`, and a failed registry update rolls the folder back.
